1: # Kallar
2: 
3: ### A multiscript typeface that blooms.
4: 
5: ![Kallar — five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kallar_multiscript.png)
6: 
7: ![License: OFL 1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-OFL%201.1-ee7944)
8: ![Scripts: 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/scripts-5-3d4fbf)
9: ![Variable: APER 0–100](https://img.shields.io/badge/variable-APER%200--100-7f63d6)
10: ![Colour: COLRv1](https://img.shields.io/badge/colour-COLRv1-d973a0)
11: 
12: **Kallar** is a multiscript display type system built around one idea: the
13: counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a loop is the
14: classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft petal. The
15: transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType variation
16: axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.
17: 
18: The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
19: **Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
20: script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and
21: vertical metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of design
22: stops, one Spectrum palette and one build pipeline.
23: 
24: The Malayalam branch is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh
25: Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam Computing. The four new branches are
26: built on the corresponding **Noto Sans** skeletons by the Noto Project
27: Authors. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License. The aperture
28: engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are new work by
29: the Kallar Project Authors.
30: 
31: Kallar lives at
32: [github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar](https://github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar).
33:

57: ## The idea
58: 
59: Malayalam is a script of loops. The loop head is its most recognisable
60: gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most typefaces treat that loop
61: as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.
62: 
63: At `APER 0` the counter is a classic round loop. As `APER` rises, the crown of
64: the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative space becomes a lotus petal,
65: a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows with a gentler version of the
66: same gesture, so open arches and closed loops share one rhythm. The counters
67: themselves change shape — this is outline variation, not a decorative overlay.
68: 
69: The second layer is colour. **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange
70: gradient inside the font with COLRv1 and CPAL. The gradient is defined once per
71: glyph in font units, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than
72: a set of separately coloured letters.
73: 
74: Kallar is a **display** companion, designed to be set large where the petal
75: crowns and the spectrum are visible. It is also comfortable in short text,
76: where the crowns settle into a quiet, readable rhythm.
77: 
78: ### Design principles
79: 
80: 1. **The counter is the signature.** The transform starts in the negative
81:    space, not on the outer contour.
82: 2. **One grammar, five scripts.** Scripts keep their own shaping and
83:    proportions, but share the same aperture logic.
84: 3. **Point compatibility over effects.** Masters only move existing points, so
85:    every intermediate value is a designed shape and text keeps its metrics.
86: 4. **Colour is part of the type.** The spectrum is painted by the font, not
87:    pasted on top of it.
88: 5. **Honest derivatives.** The base skeletons, their authors and their OFL
89:    licences are recorded in the fonts and in this repository.
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## Five scripts, one aperture
94: 
95: | Script | Native name | Family | Base skeleton | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
96: |---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
97: | Malayalam | **കല്ലാർ** | `Kallar` | Manjari | full block | 918 / 912 |
98: | Devanagari (Hindi) | **कल्लार** | `Kallar Devanagari` | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1117 |
99: | Tamil | **கல்லார்** | `Kallar Tamil` | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 576 |
100: | Telugu | **కల్లార్** | `Kallar Telugu` | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1247 |
101: | Kannada | **ಕಲ್ಲಾರ್** | `Kallar Kannada` | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 933 |
102: 
103: The name **Kallar** is written **കല്ലാർ** in Malayalam, **कल्लार** in
104: Devanagari, **கல்லார்** in Tamil, **కల్లార్** in Telugu and **ಕಲ್ಲಾರ್** in
105: Kannada.
106: 
107: “Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
108: Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
109: own script plus the Latin, digits and punctuation inherited from the base.
110: 
111: ![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kallar_multiscript_axis.png)
112: 
113: ### Script-specific profiles
114: 
115: Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
116: single counter grammar:
117: 
118: - **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
119:   headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
120: - **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
121:   more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and inner curves.
122: - **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
123:   loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
124: - The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
125:   punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in the base style. The axis changes
126:   the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.
127: 
128: The per-script specimens show the full system:
129: 
130: | | |
131: |---|---|
132: | ![Devanagari](proofs/kallar_devanagari.png) | ![Tamil](proofs/kallar_tamil.png) |
133: | ![Telugu](proofs/kallar_telugu.png) | ![Kannada](proofs/kallar_kannada.png) |
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## The APER axis
138: 
139: ![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kallar_axis.png)
140: 
141: Every counter in Kallar can open from a classic round loop (`APER 0`) to a
142: pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis has five design stops:
143: 
144: | APER | Name | Character |
145: |---:|---|---|
146: | 0 | Round | The classic loop |
147: | 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
148: | 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
149: | 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
150: | 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |
151: 
152: ![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kallar_aper.gif)
153: 
154: The two masters share the same point topology, so every intermediate value is
155: a designed shape and HarfBuzz shaping is identical at every stop. The axis
156: changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the
157: kerning.
158: 
159: ```css
160: /* 0 = round · 50 = bloom · 100 = petal */
161: font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
162: ```
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## The Spectrum
167: 
168: ![Kallar Spectrum](proofs/kallar_gradient.png)
169: 
170: **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange gradient inside the font itself
171: with COLRv1 and CPAL. Blue sits at the crown, orange near the baseline and gold
172: in the descenders, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than a
173: set of separately coloured letters. Regular and Bold Spectrum builds ship for
174: every script.
175: 
176: | Stop | Colour | Role |
177: |---:|---|---|
178: | 0.00 | `#181E5C` | deep indigo |
179: | 0.20 | `#2B3FB0` | blue |
180: | 0.40 | `#5C64DB` | periwinkle |
181: | 0.58 | `#A06CD2` | violet |
182: | 0.74 | `#D973A0` | pink |
183: | 0.88 | `#EE7944` | Sarvam orange |
184: | 1.00 | `#F9C36D` | warm gold |
185: 
186: Clients with COLRv1 support paint the gradient; clients without it fall back
187: to the monochrome outlines. The gradient is clipped to each glyph outline and
188: runs from `y=620` to `y=-120` in font units.
189: 
190: The spectrum is an homage to the lotus-and-gateway visual language of
191: [Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand). This project is independent and is
192: not affiliated with or endorsed by Sarvam AI.
193:

210: ## Character set
211: 
212: ![Kallar character sheet](proofs/kallar_glyphs.png)
213: 
214: The Malayalam family covers the complete Malayalam block plus Latin:
215: 
216: - 36 consonants, 16 independent vowels, all vowel signs and chillus
217: - Common conjuncts, reph forms, ya/va post-base signs
218: - Malayalam digits ൦–൯ and historical numerals ൰–൵
219: - Rare letters (ഩ ഺ ഽ ൏), chandrabindu, visarga, virama
220: - Latin uppercase/lowercase, digits, punctuation and common accents
221: - **918 glyphs** in Regular, **912** in Bold
222: 
223: The multiscript families retain the full cmap and GSUB coverage of their
224: bases: Devanagari includes the Devanagari block, Devanagari Extended and the
225: Vedic extensions supported by Noto; Tamil, Telugu and Kannada include their
226: full blocks. Coverage is verified codepoint by codepoint in
227: `tests/test_multiscript.py`.
228: 
229: | Family | Script cmap | Colour glyphs (Spectrum) |
230: |---|---:|---:|
231: | Kallar (Malayalam) | full block | 913 Regular / 907 Bold |
232: | Kallar Devanagari | 201 | 1111 |
233: | Kallar Tamil | 72 | 570 |
234: | Kallar Telugu | 100 | 1242 |
235: | Kallar Kannada | 91 | 928 |

239: ## The family
240: 
241: Each of the five script families ships the same seven styles. All files are
242: available as TTF and WOFF2.

276: ## Download
277: 
278: The latest TTF and WOFF2 builds live in [`fonts/`](fonts/). The multiscript
279: specimen is [`specimen/multiscript.html`](specimen/multiscript.html); the
280: vector PDF is
281: [`proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf`](proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf).
282: Open the HTML directly, or serve both specimens with:
283: 
284: ```bash
285: make serve   # http://localhost:8000
286: ```
287: 
288: For most web projects, use the WOFF2 variable fonts. For desktop design apps,
289: install the TTF variable fonts. If an app does not expose custom variation
290: axes, use the static `Round` (APER 0) or `Petal` (APER 100) instances.
291: 
292: > **Note:** the five script families are deliberately separate fonts. There is
293: > no single merged all-script TTF, because each script has its own GSUB/GPOS
294: > tables, glyph names and vertical metrics.
295:

297: 
298: ## Using Kallar
299: 
300: ### Web
301: 
302: ```css
303: @font-face {
304:   font-family: "Kallar";
305:   src: url("Kallar-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
306:   font-weight: 400;
307:   font-display: swap;
308: }
309: 
310: @font-face {
311:   font-family: "Kallar";
312:   src: url("Kallar-Bold.woff2") format("woff2");
313:   font-weight: 700;
314:   font-display: swap;
315: }
316: 
317: .bloom {
318:   font-family: "Kallar";
319:   font-weight: 700;
320:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100; /* 0 = round, 100 = petal */
321: }
322: ```
323: 
324: ### Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada
325: 
326: ```css
327: @font-face {
328:   font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
329:   src: url("KallarDevanagari-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
330:   font-weight: 400;
331: }
332: 
333: .deva {
334:   font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
335:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
336: }
337: ```
338: 
339: ### Mixed-script copy
340: 
341: Stack the families. The browser picks the first family that supports each
342: character — the Malayalam family handles Malayalam and the shared Latin, and
343: the script families fill in the rest:
344: 
345: ```css
346: .multiscript {
347:   font-family:
348:     "Kallar",
349:     "Kallar Devanagari",
350:     "Kallar Tamil",
351:     "Kallar Telugu",
352:     "Kallar Kannada",
353:     sans-serif;
354:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
355: }
356: ```
357: 
358: ### Colour
359: 
360: Use `Kallar-SpectrumRegular` / `Kallar-Spectrum`, or the corresponding
361: `Kallar<Script>-Spectrum*` builds. Clients with COLRv1 support paint the
362: gradient; clients without it fall back to the monochrome outlines.
363: 
364: ```css
365: .spectrum {
366:   font-family: "Kallar Spectrum", "Kallar", sans-serif;
367:   font-weight: 700;
368: }
369: ```
370: 
371: ### JavaScript
372: 
373: ```js
374: const title = document.querySelector(".bloom");
375: title.style.fontVariationSettings = '"APER" 65';
376: ```
377: 
378: ### HarfBuzz
379: 
380: ```python
381: import uharfbuzz as hb
382: 
383: blob = hb.Blob.from_file_path("KallarDevanagari-Regular.ttf")
384: face = hb.Face(blob)
385: font = hb.Font(face)
386: font.set_variations({"APER": 65})
387: ```
388: 
389: ### The APER value
390: 
391: | Value | Use it for |
392: |---:|---|
393: | 0 | A conventional, round text cut |
394: | 25–50 | A subtle display lift |
395: | 50–75 | A clear petal silhouette |
396: | 100 | The full lotus display cut (default) |

400: ## Building from source
401: 
402: The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1.
403: 
404: ```bash
405: make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
406: make kallar          # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
407: make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
408: make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
409: make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
410: make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen
411: make pdf-multiscript # multiscript vector PDF specimen
412: make qa              # fontbakery on Malayalam Regular and Bold
413: make qa-multiscript  # fontbakery on the four new Regular/Bold families
414: ```
415: 
416: `make kamalam` remains as a deprecated alias for the old v1.000 target name.
417: 
418: ### Source layout
419: 
420: | Path | What it is |
421: |---|---|
422: | `tools/kallar.py` | The aperture engine, Malayalam build, spectrum, instances |
423: | `tools/multiscript.py` | The Devanagari/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada build driver |
424: | `tools/specimen.py` | Malayalam proof images and brand mockups |
425: | `tools/specimen_multiscript.py` | Multiscript hero, axis and script sheets |
426: | `tools/specimen_html.py` | Self-contained Malayalam HTML specimen |
427: | `tools/specimen_multiscript_html.py` | Self-contained multiscript HTML specimen |
428: | `tools/pdf.py` | Chromium PDF printer |
429: | `sources/base/` | Manjari and Noto Sans source fonts + upstream OFL texts |
430: | `tests/test_kallar.py` | Malayalam shaping, variation and colour tests |
431: | `tests/test_multiscript.py` | Multiscript axes, metadata, coverage and colour tests |
432: 
433: ### Reproducible builds
434: 
435: `head.created` and `head.modified` are pinned to a fixed date and
436: `recalcTimestamp` is disabled. Repeated `make kallar` and `make multiscript`
437: runs produce byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is
438: deterministic too.

442: ## Testing and QA
443: 
444: - HarfBuzz shaping across `APER 0`, `50` and `100` for every script — identical
445:   glyph sequences and advances, no `.notdef` in any test case.
446: - Full cmap coverage of each base script, plus conjuncts, matras, reph forms
447:   and the Devanagari Vedic extensions supported by the base.
448: - Outline variation at the two extremes, and a guard that Latin stays
449:   untouched in the script families.
450: - Static Round/Petal instances differ from each other and carry the correct
451:   names; COLRv1/CPAL paint graphs are present in every Spectrum build.
452: - Fontbakery universal: **0 FAIL** on all eight multiscript Regular/Bold
453:   variable fonts. The same documented custom-axis and Bold/`fsSelection`
454:   exclusions as Malayalam are used, plus numeric STAT labels that stay inside
455:   the Windows 31-character limit. Inherited Noto warnings are listed in
456:   [NOTES.md](NOTES.md).
457: - Both HTML specimens and the COLRv1 gradient were verified in headless
458:   Chromium 156; the shared APER slider drives all four script families.
459: - Byte-identical repeat builds for `make kallar` and `make multiscript`.

463: ## Design notes
464: 
465: The full design and engineering rationale is in [NOTES.md](NOTES.md),
466: including:
467: 
468: - why Manjari and Noto Sans are the skeletons;
469: - the exact aperture parameters for each script;
470: - why Devanagari needs an absolute headline freeze;
471: - how the GSUB closure keeps Latin in the base style;
472: - metrics, reproducibility, fontbakery exclusions and known limits.
473: 
474: The short version:
475: 
476: | Script | Profile |
477: |---|---|
478: | Malayalam | Full hole-and-crown warp; the original Kallar cut |
479: | Devanagari | Counters-only below an absolute headline freeze |
480: | Tamil | Gentler profile concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
481: | Telugu | Full hole-and-crown warp |
482: | Kannada | Full hole-and-crown warp |

1: # Kallar — design & engineering notes
2: 
3: ## 1. The idea
4: 
5: Malayalam is a loop script. The loop head (തല) is the script's most recognisable
6: gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most Malayalam typefaces treat
7: that loop as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.
8: 
9: At `APER 0` the counter is the classic round loop inherited from Manjari. As
10: `APER` rises, the crown of the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative
11: space becomes a lotus petal / a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows
12: with a gentler version of the same gesture, so open arches (മ, ന, ത) and closed
13: loops (ക, ഖ, ങ) share one rhythm. The result is not a decorative overlay; the
14: *counters themselves* change shape.
15: 
16: The second layer is colour. Sarvam's identity uses a blue → orange spectrum and
17: a lotus/gateway monogram. Kallar Spectrum carries a vertical
18: blue → orange gradient inside the font with COLRv1, clipped to each glyph. At
19: text sizes the tops are blue, the baseline zone is pink/orange and the
20: descenders are gold — one continuous field across the text block.
21: 
22: The family is deliberately a **display** companion, not a replacement for a
23: text face. It is designed to be set large, where the petal crowns and the
24: spectrum are visible.
25: 
26: ## 2. Why Manjari is the skeleton
27: 
28: The project's first two versions attempted a fully from-scratch parametric
29: Malayalam design (`legacy/`, `tools/glyphs_ml.py`). That work proved the
30: pipeline and the shaping stack, but matching the structural subtlety of a
31: production Malayalam face — the exact placement of loops, the counter rhythm,
32: the conjunct grammar — is a years-long project. For the production release we
33: made a deliberate choice:
34: 
35: - use **Manjari** (SIL OFL 1.1, by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC) as the
36:   structural foundation, because its loops and proportions are already a
37:   high-quality expression of the script;
38: - keep the base unmodified in `sources/base/` and record the transformation in
39:   code;
40: - do the new work where it is genuinely new: the aperture engine, the variable
41:   axis, the colour build, the metrics and the specimen.
42: 
43: This is a common and legitimate model in type design: a new face can share a
44: skeleton with an established one while having a distinct design language. The
45: derived font is renamed, the original copyright is preserved in the name table,
46: and the build is reproducible. The OFL permits this; the attribution is in the
47: font metadata, the README, the specimen and `AUTHORS.md`.
48: 
49: ## 3. The aperture transform
50: 
51: ### 3.1 Point compatibility
52: 
53: `varLib` requires masters with identical point topology. The transform
54: therefore only **moves existing TrueType points**; it never adds or removes
55: contours or points. Both the round master and the petal master start from the
56: same scaled Manjari source:
57: 
58: ```
59: Manjari-Regular.ttf (2048 UPM)
60:   └─ scale_upem → 1000 UPM
61:        ├─ round master: no warp
62:        └─ petal master: petal_warp()
63: ```
64: 
65: Because the point count, contour order and glyph order are unchanged, the
66: `gvar` deltas are exact and interpolation is smooth at every intermediate
67: value.
68: 
69: ### 3.2 Counter crowns
70: 
71: For each hole contour:
72: 
73: 1. compute its bbox and centre;
74: 2. for each point in the upper 55% of the hole, compute `u = (x-cx)/rx`,
75:    `v = (y-ymin)/h`, `t = (v-0.45)/0.55`;
76: 3. find the nearest outer-contour point with a KD-tree;
77: 4. lift the point by
78:    `bump * (1-u²) * t²`, where `bump = min(hole_bump, cap_frac * distance)`;
79: 5. pinch it horizontally by `pin * u * t²` to sharpen the crown.
80: 
81: The distance cap is essential. Manjari's strokes are ~65 units at 1000 UPM; an
82: uncapped 110-unit lift would push the counter through the outer contour and
83: create a hairline notch. Capping at 55% of the nearest stroke thickness makes
84: the petal safe on every glyph, including the tiny loops of ഇ, ഈ, ഠ and the
85: historical numerals. The cap varies per point, so the warp stays smooth.
86: 
87: ### 3.3 Outer crowns
88: 
89: Open counters (മ, ന, ത, യ, …) are not holes; their inner edge is part of the
90: outer contour. To bring them into the same language, the engine finds local
91: maxima on every outer contour in the upper half of the glyph and applies a
92: smooth Gaussian lift:
93: 
94: ```
95: wy = clamp((y - (gymin+0.35*gh)) / (0.65*gh), 0, 1)
96: pull = exp(-((x-px)/sigma)^2) * wy^2
97: y += peak_bump * pull
98: x -= 0.5 * pinch * (x-px) * exp(...) * wy
99: ```
100: 
101: `sigma` is relative to the contour width, so wide letters get a broad crown and
102: narrow letters a tighter one. The lift is subtle enough that the counters stay
103: open and readable.
104: 
105: ### 3.4 Parameters at 1000 UPM
106: 
107: | parameter | value | role |
108: |---|---:|---|
109: | `hole_bump` | 110 | maximum counter crown lift |
110: | `peak_bump` | 40 | outer crown lift |
111: | `sigma_f` | 0.28 | crown width relative to contour width |
112: | `pinch` | 0.055 | horizontal sharpening |
113: | `cap_frac` | 0.55 | maximum lift as a fraction of local stroke |
114: 
115: The static `APER 0`, `50`, `100` instances are produced with
116: `fontTools.varLib.instancer`.
117: 
118: ## 4. Metrics
119: 
120: The base is scaled to 1000 UPM. The final metrics are:
121: 
122: - `sTypoAscender = 800`, `sTypoDescender = -300`, `sTypoLineGap = 0`
123: - `hhea.ascent = 800`, `hhea.descent = -300`, `lineGap = 0`
124: - `usWinAscent = 1100`, `usWinDescent = 700` (the real glyph extents are
125:   roughly -614…1075, so the win metrics never clip)
126: - `USE_TYPO_METRICS` (OS/2 fsSelection bit 7) is set.
127: - The vertical metrics are intentionally generous: Malayalam marks, chillus
128:   and the Latin superscripts extend above the nominal ascender.
129: 
130: Manjari's advances, kerning and GSUB/GPOS are preserved. The warp only changes
131: outline coordinates, so spacing and shaping stay stable across the axis.
132: 
133: ## 5. COLRv1 spectrum
134: 
135: The Spectrum builds start from the variable Regular and Bold and add:
136: 
137: - `CPAL` with a 7-entry palette:
138:   `#181E5C`, `#2B3FB0`, `#5C64DB`, `#A06CD2`, `#D973A0`, `#EE7944`, `#F9C36D`.
139: - `COLR` version 1 with one `BaseGlyphPaintRecord` per non-empty glyph:
140:   `PaintGlyph(glyph)` → `PaintLinearGradient`.
141: - The gradient runs from `(0, 620)` to `(0, -120)`, with the rotation point
142:   `(500, 620)` (perpendicular to the gradient direction). The gradient is in
143:   font units and is clipped by the glyph outline. This range puts blue at the
144:   top of the body, orange near the baseline and gold in the descenders.
145: - 907 glyphs carry a paint record in the Bold build and 913 in the Regular
146:   build; the rest fall back to monochrome.
147: 
148: Browsers/apps with COLRv1 (Chrome, Edge, Figma, recent Safari) paint the
149: gradient; apps without it render the base outlines. The specimen also shows a
150: CSS gradient-clipped version so the visual idea is visible everywhere.
151:

153:

157: - `STAT` axis values Round / Bloom / Petal;

161: - coverage of every assigned Malayalam codepoint;
162: - outline variation between the extremes;

175: ## 7. Fontbakery notes
176: 
177: The Regular font passes `fontbakery check-universal` with two exclusions that
178: do not apply to this design:
179: 
180: - `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` assumes a registered `wght`/`wdth`
181:   axis; Kallar's only axis is the custom `APER`.
182: - `alt_caron` is a Czech/Slovak-specific check that wants `ď` to use a
183:   non-standard caron glyph. The Latin `ď` here uses a combining caron, which
184:   is typographically correct; the check is not relevant to a Malayalam face.
185: 
186: For the Bold and Spectrum builds, `opentype/fsselection` and
187: `opentype/mac_style` also need excluding because fontbakery infers "Bold"
188: from a `wght` axis or a filename convention and cannot see the custom-axis
189: Bold style; the OS/2 and `head` values themselves are correct. Run the QA
190: target with:
191: 
192: ```bash
193: make qa
194: ```
195: 
196: The specimen HTML and COLRv1 paint were verified in headless Chromium 156.
197: 
198: ## 8. Known limits / next work
199: 
200: - The transform is derived from Manjari's skeleton; it is not a new
201:   construction from a blank page. A future release could redraw the skeleton
202:   from the same aperture grammar while keeping the axis.
203: - The Spectrum gradient is static; a `COLRv1` variable gradient tied to `APER`
204:   would be the next step.
205: - A `wght` axis would need point-compatible masters from a variable source
206:   (Noto Sans Malayalam is a candidate) or a carefully offset master.
207: - The display cut is optimised for large sizes. A text-optimised cut with
208:   smaller petal lifts and looser spacing is planned.
209: 
210: ## 9. The multiscript extension
211: 
212: ### 9.1 Why separate families
213: 
214: Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face; it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
215: Kannada glyphs. A literal Manjari derivative therefore cannot cover those
216: scripts. The multiscript release uses one OFL skeleton per script and keeps the
217: same derivative model: rename, preserve the upstream copyright, record the
218: base, and do the new work in the aperture engine, axis, Spectrum, metrics and
219: specimens.
220: 
221: The four new families are deliberately separate variable fonts rather than one
222: merged font. Scripts have different GSUB/GPOS tables, glyph names, mark
223: attachments and vertical metrics; merging them would create conflicts in
224: shared Latin, punctuation and mark glyphs. Separate families also match how
225: Anek, Noto and most multiscript systems ship, and let each script keep its own
226: line height.
227: 
228: ### 9.2 Sources
229: 
230: | Branch | Base | Upstream |
231: |---|---|---|
232: | Devanagari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari |
233: | Tamil | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil |
234: | Telugu | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu |
235: | Kannada | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada |
236: 
237: The variable bases are instantiated at `wght=400/700`, `wdth=100`, scaled to
238: 1000 UPM (they are already 1000), stripped of hinting and variation tables, and
239: given the Kallar name/metrics. The vendored files and SHA-256 checksums are in
240: `sources/base/README.md`.
241: 
242: ### 9.3 Script-specific aperture profiles
243: 
244: The warp is still point-preserving, but the profiles differ because the
245: scripts do not share one counter grammar.
246: 
247: | Script | hole_bump | peak_bump | freeze | sigma_f | Notes |
248: |---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
249: | Devanagari | 110 | 60 | absolute y=545, fade 120 | 0.22 | Keeps the shirorekha straight; only loops below it open |
250: | Tamil | 100 | 25 | top 18% | 0.30 | Gentler; concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
251: | Telugu | 110 | 40 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
252: | Kannada | 110 | 36 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
253: 
254: `PETAL_WARP` now supports `only` (a glyph-name set), `freeze_top` (fraction),
255: `freeze_above` (absolute y), `freeze_fade`, `peak_max_frac`/`peak_max_y` and
256: `valley_bump`. With the defaults these are no-ops, which is why the Malayalam
257: build remains byte-identical.
258: 
259: The **absolute freeze** is the important Devanagari detail. Devanagari base
260: letters share a headline at roughly y=570–622; freezing above y=545 leaves the
261: headline and its junctions untouched, while the counter tops below 545 can
262: rise. A 120-unit fade avoids a hard step at the freeze boundary. The first
263: attempt used a per-glyph percentage freeze and a wide Gaussian, which pulled
264: the headline at the stem junctions; the absolute freeze plus a narrower
265: `sigma_f=0.22` fixed it.
266: 
267: ### 9.4 Glyph filtering
268: 
269: `petal_warp` accepts `only`, a set of glyph names. `tools/multiscript.py`
270: computes that set with `fontTools.subset`: it starts from the script's
271: codepoints and closes over GSUB, so conjuncts, half forms, reph forms,
272: contextual variants and matras are included. Latin, punctuation and unrelated
273: glyphs are left in the base style. This is why the Latin in the new families
274: stays Noto Sans, while the script outline changes.
275: 
276: The closure sizes (excluding `.notdef`) are 735 Devanagari, 166 Tamil, 723
277: Telugu and 414 Kannada glyphs.
278: 
279: ### 9.5 Metrics
280: 
281: The new families use the base typographic ascender/descender, but the win
282: metrics are computed from the actual outline extents:
283: 
284: ```
285: usWinAscent  = max(sTypoAscender, ceil(yMax) + 50)
286: usWinDescent = max(-sTypoDescender, ceil(-yMin) + 50)
287: ```
288: 
289: Devanagari uses `sTypoAscender=1000` (rather than Noto's 896) because its
290: Vedic marks reach y=1347 and fontbakery's ascender check wants more room. The
291: other families keep their base ascenders: Tamil 870, Telugu 869, Kannada 809.
292: All set `USE_TYPO_METRICS`.
293: 
294: ### 9.6 Testing and QA
295: 
296: `tests/test_multiscript.py` checks, for all four scripts:
297: 
298: - `fvar` `APER=0…100`, default 100, and STAT values 0/50/100;
299: - the Noto copyright and Kallar modification notice in name ID 0, the Noto
300:   designer credit in name ID 9, and the OFL notice in name ID 13;
301: - shaping of every case, display word and paragraph at APER 0/50/100, with

    cps = set()
    for table in font["cmap"].tables:
        if not table.isUnicode():
            continue
        for cp in table.cmap:
            if any(lo <= cp <= hi for lo, hi in ranges):
                cps.add(cp)
    return cps

    Using fontTools' subsetter closure means conjuncts, half forms, reph forms

    unrelated glyphs are left in the base style.

    opts.layout_features = ["*"]
    opts.notdef_outline = True
    opts.recalc_bounds = False

    subsetter = subset.Subsetter(opts)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Kallar — the aperture-variable Malayalam display family.

Design idea
-----------
Every Malayalam loop/arch is treated as a *gateway*: a round base that rises
to a soft lotus-petal crown.  The transformation is parametric and applied to
a proven open-source Malayalam skeleton (Manjari by Santhosh Thottingal /
SMC, OFL-1.1).  It is exposed as the ``APER`` (Aperture) variation axis:

    APER 0    classic round Manjari-derived forms
    APER 100  the full petal / gateway display cut (default)

The same outlines are then given a COLRv1 blue→orange spectrum in the
``Kallar Spectrum`` build, referencing Sarvam's visual language
without copying its wordmark.

All masters are point-compatible: the warp only moves existing TrueType
points, so varLib can interpolate between them cleanly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import copy
import math
import os
import sys

from fontTools.designspaceLib import (
    AxisDescriptor,
    DesignSpaceDocument,
    InstanceDescriptor,
    SourceDescriptor,
)
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
from fontTools.ttLib.scaleUpem import scale_upem
from fontTools.varLib import build as varlib_build
from fontTools.varLib.instancer import instantiateVariableFont
from fontTools.colorLib.builder import buildCOLR, buildCPAL
from fontTools.ttLib.tables import otTables as ot
from fontTools.otlLib.builder import buildStatTable
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE = os.path.join(ROOT, "sources", "base")
MASTERS = os.path.join(ROOT, "sources", "masters")
FONTS = os.path.join(ROOT, "fonts")
PROOFS = os.path.join(ROOT, "proofs")

UPEM = 1000

# Reproducible builds: freeze the head timestamps so repeated builds are
# byte-identical unless the design actually changes.
from fontTools.misc.timeTools import timestampFromString  # noqa: E402
FIXED_TIME = timestampFromString("Mon Nov  9 00:00:00 2026")

# Design constants (in 1000-unit em)
HOLE_BUMP = 110.0       # how far a counter crown rises at APER=100
PEAK_BUMP = 40.0        # how far an outer contour crown rises
SIGMA_F = 0.28          # width of the peak-sharpening field
PINCH = 0.055           # horizontal pinch at the crown
CAP_FRAC = 0.55         # max counter movement as a fraction of local stroke


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# geometry helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def contour_area(pts):
    a = 0.0
    for j in range(len(pts)):
        x0, y0 = pts[j]
        x1, y1 = pts[(j + 1) % len(pts)]
        a += x0 * y1 - x1 * y0
    return a / 2.0


def _split_contours(glyph):
    start = 0
    contours = []
    for end in glyph.endPtsOfContours:
        contours.append((start, end))
        start = end + 1
    return contours


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the petal warp
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def petal_warp(font: TTFont, hole_bump=HOLE_BUMP, peak_bump=PEAK_BUMP,
               sigma_f=SIGMA_F, pinch=PINCH, cap_frac=CAP_FRAC,
               only=None, freeze_top=None, peak_max_frac=None,
               freeze_above=None, peak_max_y=None, freeze_fade=None,
               valley_bump=0.0):
    """Move counters and outer crowns into lotus-petal shapes.

    The operation is point-preserving: only coordinates change, so two
    masters warped with different parameters remain interpolation-compatible.

    ``only`` restricts the transform to a set of glyph names.  ``freeze_top``
    is a fraction of the glyph height and ``freeze_above`` an absolute y:
    points above that line do not move, which keeps a headline (Devanagari
    shirorekha) perfectly straight.  ``freeze_fade`` softens the transition
    over that many units below the freeze line.  ``peak_max_frac`` /
    ``peak_max_y`` limit outer-contour peak candidates to below that height.
    ``valley_bump`` optionally pulls rounded lower loops into downward petals.
    """
    glyf = font["glyf"]
    for gname in font.getGlyphOrder():
        if only is not None and gname not in only:
            continue
        if gname not in glyf:
            continue
        glyph = glyf[gname]
        if glyph.numberOfContours <= 0:
            continue
        coords = glyph.coordinates
        new = copy.deepcopy(coords)
        contours = _split_contours(glyph)
        allpts = [coords[i] for i in range(len(coords))]
        gymin = min(p[1] for p in allpts)
        gymax = max(p[1] for p in allpts)
        gh = max(1.0, gymax - gymin)
        freeze_y = None
        if freeze_above is not None:
            freeze_y = freeze_above
        elif freeze_top is not None:
            freeze_y = gymin + freeze_top * gh
        peak_y = None
        if peak_max_y is not None:
            peak_y = peak_max_y
        elif peak_max_frac is not None:
            peak_y = gymin + peak_max_frac * gh

        def move_weight(y):
            """Smooth 0..1 falloff below the freeze line."""
            if freeze_y is None:
                return 1.0
            if y > freeze_y:
                return 0.0
            if not freeze_fade:
                return 1.0
            return min(1.0, (freeze_y - y) / freeze_fade)

        # All outer-contour points, used to cap counter movement so a petal
        # can never break through the stroke.
        outer_pts = []
        for s, e in contours:
            pts = [coords[i] for i in range(s, e + 1)]
            if contour_area(pts) < 0:
                outer_pts.extend(pts)
        tree = cKDTree(outer_pts) if outer_pts else None

        for s, e in contours:
            pts = [coords[i] for i in range(s, e + 1)]
            ar = contour_area(pts)
            xmin = min(p[0] for p in pts)
            xmax = max(p[0] for p in pts)
            ymin = min(p[1] for p in pts)
            ymax = max(p[1] for p in pts)
            cx = (xmin + xmax) / 2.0
            w = max(1.0, (xmax - xmin) / 2.0)
            h = ymax - ymin

            if ar > 0:  # counter
                if h <= 20 or w <= 20 or tree is None:
                    continue
                for i in range(s, e + 1):
                    x, y = coords[i]
                    weight = move_weight(y)
                    if weight <= 0:
                        continue
                    u = (x - cx) / w
                    v = (y - ymin) / h
                    if v <= 0.45:
                        continue
                    t = (v - 0.45) / 0.55
                    dist = tree.query((x, y))[0]
                    bump = min(hole_bump, cap_frac * dist) * weight
                    pin = min(pinch * w, 0.30 * dist) * weight
                    new[i] = (x - pin * u * t * t,
                              y + bump * (1.0 - u * u) * t * t)
            else:  # outer contour: sharpen local crowns
                n = len(pts)
                peaks = []
                for j in range(n):
                    y0 = pts[(j - 1) % n][1]
                    y1 = pts[j][1]
                    y2 = pts[(j + 1) % n][1]
                    if y1 >= y0 and y1 >= y2 and y1 > gymin + 0.45 * gh:
                        if peak_y is not None and y1 > peak_y:
                            continue
                        if (not peaks or
                                abs(pts[j][0] - peaks[-1][0]) > 0.15 * (xmax - xmin)):
                            peaks.append((pts[j][0], y1))
                for px, py in peaks:
                    sigma = max(30.0, (xmax - xmin) * sigma_f)
                    for i in range(s, e + 1):
                        x, y = coords[i]
                        weight = move_weight(y)
                        if weight <= 0:
                            continue
                        wy = max(0.0, (y - (gymin + 0.35 * gh)) / (gh * 0.65))
                        wy = min(1.0, wy)
                        d = (x - px) / sigma
                        pull = math.exp(-d * d) * (wy * wy)
                        new[i] = (new[i][0] - 0.5 * pinch * (x - px) *
                                  math.exp(-d * d) * wy * weight,
                                  new[i][1] + peak_bump * pull * weight)

                if valley_bump:
                    valleys = []
                    for j in range(n):
                        y0 = pts[(j - 1) % n][1]
                        y1 = pts[j][1]
                        y2 = pts[(j + 1) % n][1]
                        if y1 < y0 and y1 < y2 and y1 < gymin + 0.55 * gh:
                            if (not valleys or
                                    abs(pts[j][0] - valleys[-1][0]) >
                                    0.15 * (xmax - xmin)):
                                valleys.append((pts[j][0], y1))
                    for px, py in valleys:
                        sigma = max(30.0, (xmax - xmin) * sigma_f)
                        for i in range(s, e + 1):
                            x, y = coords[i]
                            weight = move_weight(y)
                            if weight <= 0:
                                continue
                            wy = max(0.0, (gymin + 0.55 * gh - y) / (0.55 * gh))
                            wy = min(1.0, wy)
                            d = (x - px) / sigma
                            pull = math.exp(-d * d) * (wy * wy)
                            new[i] = (new[i][0] - 0.5 * pinch * (x - px) *
                                      math.exp(-d * d) * wy * weight,
                                      new[i][1] - valley_bump * pull * weight)
        glyph.coordinates = new
        glyph.recalcBounds(glyf)

def build_script(key):
    script = SCRIPTS[key]
    os.makedirs(MASTERS, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FONTS, exist_ok=True)

    paths = []
    vfs = {}
    for weight in (400, 700):
        style = style_for(weight)
        round_path = instantiate_base(script, weight)
        if weight == 400:
            cps = script_codepoints(TTFont(round_path), script["ranges"])
            glyphs = script_glyphs(round_path, cps)
            print(f"{key}: {len(cps)} codepoints, {len(glyphs)} glyphs in closure")
        petal_path = os.path.join(
            MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}-Petal.ttf"
        )
        make_petal(round_path, petal_path, glyphs, script["warp"])
        ds_path = os.path.join(MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}.designspace")
        build_designspace(
            round_path, petal_path, ds_path,
            family=script["family"], style=style,
        )
        vf_path = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}.ttf")
        build_vf(
            ds_path, vf_path,
            family=script["family"], style=style,
            metrics=script["metrics"],
            copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
            designer=designer_for(script),
            url=PROJECT_URL,
            stat_values=[
                dict(value=0, name="0", flags=0x2),
                dict(value=50, name="50"),
                dict(value=100, name="100"),
            ],
        )
        paths.append(vf_path)
        vfs[weight] = vf_path

    # COLRv1 Spectrum, Regular and Bold
    spectrum_reg = os.path.join(
        FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-SpectrumRegular.ttf"
    )
    spectrum_bold = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Spectrum.ttf")
    add_spectrum(
        vfs[400], spectrum_reg,
        family=f"{script['family']} Spectrum", style="Regular", weight=400,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    add_spectrum(
        vfs[700], spectrum_bold,
        family=f"{script['family']} Spectrum", style="Bold", weight=700,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    paths.extend([spectrum_reg, spectrum_bold])

    # Static APER instances, following the Malayalam naming model.
    round_static = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Round.ttf")
    petal_static = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Petal.ttf")
    bold_petal = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-BoldPetal.ttf")
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[400], round_static, {"APER": 0},
        f"{script['family']} Round", "Regular",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[400], petal_static, {"APER": 100},
        f"{script['family']} Petal", "Regular",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[700], bold_petal, {"APER": 100},
        f"{script['family']} Petal", "Bold",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    paths.extend([round_static, petal_static, bold_petal])

    for path in paths:
        to_woff2(path)
    print(f"{key}: wrote {len(paths)} TTF + WOFF2 files")
    return paths

def set_metrics(font: TTFont, weight=400, asc=None, desc=None,
                win_asc=None, win_desc=None, auto_win=False,
                underline_position=None, underline_thickness=None):
    os2 = font["OS/2"]
    hhea = font["hhea"]
    head = font["head"]
    head.fontRevision = 1.1
    head.created = FIXED_TIME
    head.modified = FIXED_TIME
    # Minimal smart-dropout prep.  The font has no TT hinting otherwise;
    # this keeps legacy rasterizers on the smart-dropout path.
    from fontTools.ttLib.tables import ttProgram
    from fontTools.ttLib import newTable
    prep = newTable("prep")
    prep.program = ttProgram.Program()
    prep.program.fromBytecode(bytes([
        0xB8, 0x01, 0xFF, 0x85,  # PUSHW 0x01FF; SCANCTRL
        0xB0, 0x04, 0x8D,        # PUSHB 0x04; SCANTYPE
    ]))
    font["prep"] = prep
    asc = 800 if asc is None else asc
    desc = -300 if desc is None else desc
    if auto_win:
        glyf = font["glyf"]
        extents = []
        for gname in font.getGlyphOrder():
            if gname not in glyf:
                continue
            g = glyf[gname]
            if getattr(g, "numberOfContours", 0) == 0:
                continue
            extents.append((g.yMin, g.yMax))
        ymin = min(e[0] for e in extents)
        ymax = max(e[1] for e in extents)
        win_asc = max(asc, int(math.ceil(ymax)) + 50)
        win_desc = max(-desc, int(math.ceil(-ymin)) + 50)
    else:
        win_asc = 1100 if win_asc is None else win_asc
        win_desc = 700 if win_desc is None else win_desc
    os2.sTypoAscender = asc
    os2.sTypoDescender = desc
    os2.sTypoLineGap = 0
    os2.usWinAscent = win_asc
    os2.usWinDescent = win_desc
    os2.usWeightClass = weight
    os2.achVendID = "KLLR"
    # bit 0 = italic, bit 5 = bold, bit 6 = regular.  The base fonts differ in
    # which of these they set, so clear all three before setting the style bit.
    os2.fsSelection = (os2.fsSelection & ~0x61) | (0x20 if weight >= 700 else 0x40)
    os2.fsSelection |= 0x80  # USE_TYPO_METRICS
    hhea.ascent = asc
    hhea.descent = desc
    hhea.lineGap = 0
    head.macStyle = 1 if weight >= 700 else 0
    # neutral, upright font
    font["post"].italicAngle = 0.0
    font["post"].underlinePosition = (
        -100 if underline_position is None else underline_position
    )
    font["post"].underlineThickness = (
        50 if underline_thickness is None else underline_thickness
    )
    font["post"].isFixedPitch = 0


def add_case_pairs(font: TTFont):
    """Add the two Latin case pairs Manjari omits (ď, Ǒ).

    Manjari has Ď and ǒ but not their lower/upper counterparts.  A composite
    is enough: the base letter plus a combining caron.  The spacing U+02C7
    caron is cloned into a zero-width U+030C mark so the precomposed letters
    use a proper mark component.
    """
    glyf = font["glyf"]
    if "Dcaron" not in glyf or "caron" not in glyf:
        return

    from fontTools.ttLib.tables._g_l_y_f import Glyph, GlyphComponent

    # A zero-width combining caron for U+030C and the precomposed letters.
    if "caroncomb" not in glyf:
        order = list(font.getGlyphOrder())
        mark = copy.deepcopy(glyf["caron"])
        glyf["caroncomb"] = mark
        if "caroncomb" not in order:
            order.append("caroncomb")
        font["hmtx"].metrics["caroncomb"] = (0, 0)
        font.setGlyphOrder(order)
        glyf.glyphOrder = order
        for table in font["cmap"].tables:
            if table.isUnicode():
                table.cmap[0x030C] = "caroncomb"
        gdef = font.get("GDEF")
        if gdef is not None and getattr(gdef.table, "GlyphClassDef", None):
            gdef.table.GlyphClassDef.classDefs["caroncomb"] = 3  # mark

    # the offset used by Dcaron is already in the current UPM
    caron_offset = None
    for comp in glyf["Dcaron"].components:
        if comp.glyphName in ("caron", "caroncomb"):
            caron_offset = (comp.x, comp.y)
            comp.glyphName = "caroncomb"
            break
    for comp in glyf["ocaron"].components:
        if comp.glyphName in ("caron", "caroncomb"):
            comp.glyphName = "caroncomb"
            break
    if caron_offset is None:
        return

    for new_name, base, cp in (("dcaron", "d", 0x010F), ("Ocaron", "O", 0x01D1)):
        if new_name in glyf:
            continue
        order = list(font.getGlyphOrder())
        g = Glyph()
        g.numberOfContours = -1
        g.components = []
        for comp_name, x, y in ((base, 0, 0), ("caroncomb", *caron_offset)):
            c = GlyphComponent()
            c.flags = 0
            c.glyphName = comp_name
            c.x = x
            c.y = y
            g.components.append(c)
        g.recalcBounds(glyf)
        glyf[new_name] = g
        if new_name not in order:
            order.append(new_name)
        font["hmtx"].metrics[new_name] = font["hmtx"].metrics[base]
        font.setGlyphOrder(order)
        glyf.glyphOrder = order
        for table in font["cmap"].tables:
            if table.isUnicode():
                table.cmap[cp] = new_name
    font["maxp"].numGlyphs = len(font.getGlyphOrder())


def normalize(src, dst, petal=False, weight=400, family="Kallar",
              style="Regular", **warp_kwargs):
    font = TTFont(src)
    scale_upem(font, UPEM)
    for tag in ("prep", "fpgm", "cvt ", "VDMX", "hdmx", "LTSH"):
        if tag in font:
            del font[tag]
    if petal:
        petal_warp(font, **warp_kwargs)
    add_case_pairs(font)
    set_metrics(font, weight=weight)
    set_names(font, family, style, weight=weight)
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(dst)
    return font

def build_designspace(round_path, petal_path, out_path,
                      family="Kallar", style="Regular"):
    ds = DesignSpaceDocument()
    axis = AxisDescriptor()
    axis.name = "Aperture"
    axis.tag = "APER"
    axis.minimum = 0
    axis.default = 100
    axis.maximum = 100
    ds.addAxis(axis)

    for path, loc in [(petal_path, 100), (round_path, 0)]:
        src = SourceDescriptor()
        src.path = path
        src.name = os.path.basename(path)
        src.familyName = family
        src.styleName = style
        src.location = {"Aperture": loc}
        if loc == 100:
            src.copyInfo = True
            src.copyLib = True
            src.copyGroups = True
            src.copyFeatures = True
        ds.addSource(src)

    for name, loc, sub in [
        ("Round", 0, "Round"),
        ("Bloom", 50, "Bloom"),
        (style, 100, style),
    ]:
        inst = InstanceDescriptor()
        inst.familyName = family
        inst.styleName = sub
        inst.name = name
        inst.location = {"Aperture": loc}
        ds.addInstance(inst)

    ds.write(out_path)
    return ds


def build_vf(designspace_path, out_path, family="Kallar", style="Regular",
             metrics=None, copyright_note=None, designer=None, url=None,
             stat_values=None):
    ds = DesignSpaceDocument.fromfile(designspace_path)
    vf, _, _ = varlib_build(ds)
    set_metrics(vf, weight=700 if style == "Bold" else 400, **(metrics or {}))
    set_names(vf, family, style, weight=700 if style == "Bold" else 400,
              copyright_note=copyright_note, designer=designer, url=url)
    # A clear STAT table for the custom axis.  The default poetic names are
    # used by the Malayalam family; the multiscript build passes shorter
    # labels because the family name plus "Bloom"/"Petal" would exceed the
    # 31-character Windows limit.
    stat_values = stat_values or [
        dict(value=0, name="Round", flags=0x2),
        dict(value=50, name="Bloom"),
        dict(value=100, name="Petal"),
    ]
    buildStatTable(
        vf,
        axes=[dict(
            tag="APER",
            name="Aperture",
            ordering=0,
            values=stat_values,
        )],
        elidedFallbackName="Regular",
        macNames=False,
    )
    vf["name"].names = [n for n in vf["name"].names if n.platformID != 1]
    vf.recalcTimestamp = False
    vf.save(out_path)
    return vf

    (0.00, (0.09, 0.13, 0.42, 1.0)),   # deep indigo
    (0.20, (0.16, 0.25, 0.70, 1.0)),   # blue
    (0.40, (0.35, 0.38, 0.86, 1.0)),   # periwinkle

    (0.74, (0.85, 0.45, 0.55, 1.0)),   # pink

]


def add_spectrum(src, dst, family="Kallar Spectrum",
                 style="Bold", weight=700, y_top=620, y_bottom=-120,
                 copyright_note=None, designer=None, url=None):
    font = TTFont(src)
    glyph_map = font.getReverseGlyphMap()
    glyf = font["glyf"]
    palette = [color for _, color in SPECTRUM]

    stops = []
    for off, _ in SPECTRUM:
        stops.append({
            "StopOffset": off,
            "PaletteIndex": len(stops),
            "Alpha": 1.0,
        })

    color_glyphs = {}
    for gname in font.getGlyphOrder():
        if gname not in glyf:
            continue
        g = glyf[gname]
        if g.numberOfContours == 0:
            continue
        color_glyphs[gname] = {
            "Format": int(ot.PaintFormat.PaintGlyph),
            "Glyph": gname,
            "Paint": {
                "Format": int(ot.PaintFormat.PaintLinearGradient),
                "ColorLine": {
                    "Extend": 0,   # PAD
                    "ColorStop": stops,
                },
                "x0": 0, "y0": y_top,
                "x1": 0, "y1": y_bottom,
                "x2": 500, "y2": y_top,
            },
        }

    colr = buildCOLR(color_glyphs, version=1, glyphMap=glyph_map)
    font["COLR"] = colr
    font["CPAL"] = buildCPAL([palette], nameTable=font["name"])
    set_names(font, family, style, weight=weight,
              copyright_note=copyright_note, designer=designer, url=url)
    font["name"].names = [n for n in font["name"].names if n.platformID != 1]
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(dst)
    return font

def instantiate_with_names(src, dst, location, family, style,
                           copyright_note=None, designer=None, url=None):

        if tag in font:
            del font[tag]

              copyright_note=copyright_note, designer=designer, url=url)
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(dst)
    return font

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont

def mask(path,ch,size=1000):
    f=ImageFont.truetype(path,size)
    img=Image.new('L',(size*2,size*2),0)
    ImageDraw.Draw(img).text((50,50),ch,font=f,fill=255)
    return np.array(img)>128

def runs(mask):
    # horizontal and vertical run lengths of foreground
    out=[]
    for arr in (mask, mask.T):
        for row in arr:
            idx=np.flatnonzero(row)
            if len(idx)==0: continue
            # split into runs
            splits=np.where(np.diff(idx)>1)[0]
            starts=np.r_[idx[0], idx[splits+1]]
            ends=np.r_[idx[splits], idx[-1]]
            out.extend(ends-starts+1)
    return np.array(out)

for name,path,ch,upm in [

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
from skimage.morphology import skeletonize, medial_axis, remove_small_objects
from skimage.measure import label
import math

def glyph_mask(path,ch,size=800,pad=100):
    f=ImageFont.truetype(path,size)
    img=Image.new('L',(size*2,size*2),0)
    ImageDraw.Draw(img).text((pad,pad),ch,font=f,fill=255)
    m=np.array(img)>128
    ys,xs=np.where(m)
    return m, (xs.min(),ys.min(),xs.max(),ys.max())

def draw_skeleton(skel, width):
    # draw circles at skeleton pixels; union via max
    H,W=skel.shape
    out=np.zeros((H,W),np.uint8)
    r=width//2
    for y,x in zip(*np.where(skel)):
        y0=max(0,y-r); y1=min(H,y+r+1); x0=max(0,x-r); x1=min(W,x+r+1)
        yy,xx=np.ogrid[-r:r+1,-r:r+1]
        disk=(xx*xx+yy*yy)<=r*r
        sub=out[y0:y1,x0:x1]
        sub[disk]=255
    return out>0

for name,path,ch in [('Deva','sources/base/NotoSansDevanagari-VF.ttf','क'),('Tamil','sources/base/NotoSansTamil-VF.ttf','க')]:
    m,bbox=glyph_mask(path,ch)
    skel=medial_axis(m, return_distance=False)
    # prune short branches? just draw
    for w in [55,65,75]:
        st=draw_skeleton(skel,w)
        # compose original and stroke side by side
        h,wid=m.shape
        out=np.zeros((h,wid*2+20),np.uint8)
        out[:,:wid]=m.astype(np.uint8)*255
        out[:,wid+20:]=st.astype(np.uint8)*255
        Image.fromarray(out).save(f'/tmp/opencode/restroke_{name}_{w}.png')
    print(name,'saved')

    s=subset.Subsetter(opts)

    for t in f['cmap'].tables:
        if not t.isUnicode(): continue
        for cp in t.cmap:
            if any(lo<=cp<=hi for lo,hi in ranges): cps.add(cp)

    return set(f.getGlyphOrder())

    mh=manjari['hmtx']; dh=donor['hmtx']
    dorder=list(donor.getGlyphOrder())
    added=[]
    # first pass: copy/replace glyphs, ensuring components exist
    def ensure(name):
        if name in dg:
            # replace with manjari outline
            g=copy.deepcopy(mg[name])
            dg[name]=g
            dh.metrics[name]=mh.metrics[name]
            return
        # append
        g=copy.deepcopy(mg[name])
        dg[name]=g
        dh.metrics[name]=mh.metrics[name]
        dorder.append(name); added.append(name)
        # components
        if g.isComposite():
            for comp in g.components:
                ensure(comp.glyphName)
    for name in manjari.getGlyphOrder():
        if name in shared:
            ensure(name)
    donor.setGlyphOrder(dorder)
    dg.glyphOrder=dorder
    donor['maxp'].numGlyphs=len(dorder)
    # cmap: manjari shared cps override
    for t in manjari['cmap'].tables:
        if not t.isUnicode(): continue
        for cp,gname in t.cmap.items():
            if gname not in shared: continue
            for dt in donor['cmap'].tables:
                if dt.isUnicode() and dt.platformID==t.platformID and dt.platEncID==t.platEncID:

    return donor

from fontTools.pens.boundsPen import BoundsPen
from fontbakery.prelude import check, Message, PASS, FAIL, WARN, SKIP


@check(
    id="typoascender_exceeds_Agrave",
    rationale="""
        MacOS uses OS/2.sTypoAscender/Descender values to determine the line height
        of a font. If the sTypoAscender value is smaller than the maximum height of
        the uppercase /Agrave, the font’s sTypoAscender value is ignored, and a very
        tall line height is used instead.

        This happens on a per-font, per-style basis, so it’s possible for a font to
        have a good sTypoAscender value in one style but not in another. This can
        lead to inconsistent line heights across a typeface family.

        So, it is important to ensure that the sTypoAscender value is greater than
        the maximum height of the uppercase /Agrave in all styles of a type family.
    """,
    proposal="https://github.com/fonttools/fontbakery/issues/3170",
)
def check_typoascender_exceeds_Agrave(ttFont):
    """Checking that the typoAscender exceeds the yMax of the /Agrave."""

    # This check modifies the font file with `.draw(pen)`
    # so here we'll work with a copy of the object so that we
    # do not affect other checks:
    from copy import deepcopy

    ttFont_copy = deepcopy(ttFont)

    if "OS/2" not in ttFont_copy:
        yield FAIL, Message("lacks-OS/2", "Font file lacks OS/2 table")
        return

    glyphset = ttFont_copy.getGlyphSet()

    if "Agrave" not in glyphset and "uni00C0" not in glyphset:
        yield SKIP, Message(
            "lacks-Agrave",
            "Font file lacks the /Agrave, so it can’t be compared with typoAscender",
        )
        return

    pen = BoundsPen(glyphset)

    try:
        glyphset["Agrave"].draw(pen)
    except KeyError:
        glyphset["uni00C0"].draw(pen)

    yMax = pen.bounds[-1]

    typoAscender = ttFont_copy["OS/2"].sTypoAscender

    if typoAscender < yMax:
        yield WARN, Message(
            "typoAscender",
            f"OS/2.sTypoAscender value should be greater than {yMax},"
            f" but got {typoAscender} instead",
        )
    else:
        yield PASS, "OS/2.sTypoAscender value is greater than the yMax of /Agrave."

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Kallar multiscript — Manjari is the base of every family.

The whole Kallar system starts from the same **Manjari** skeleton.  Manjari
supplies the shared Latin, digits, punctuation, symbols, spacing, metrics and
design language of every family.  The Malayalam family is Manjari throughout.

Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, so it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
Kannada outlines.  Those four families therefore use the corresponding Noto
Sans faces as **script donors**: the donor supplies only the script-specific
letter structures (and the GSUB/GPOS rules that shape them), while every
shared glyph is transplanted from Manjari.  The donor is instantiated at the
weight that matches Manjari's pen, so the script letters sit at the same
stroke weight as the Manjari base.

Each family is a separate variable font because the scripts have different
shaping tables, glyph sets and vertical metrics.  They share the APER axis
(0..100, default 100), the five named stops, the Spectrum palette and the
static Round/Petal instances, so they can be used together as one type system.

Usage:
    python tools/multiscript.py                 # all four scripts
    python tools/multiscript.py devanagari      # one script
    python tools/multiscript.py tamil telugu    # a subset

The build is deterministic: the base fonts are vendored, the timestamps are
pinned and the transform only moves existing TrueType points, so repeated runs
produce byte-identical files.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import copy
import os
import sys

from fontTools import subset
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
from fontTools.ttLib.scaleUpem import scale_upem
from fontTools.varLib.instancer import instantiateVariableFont

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from kallar import (  # noqa: E402
    UPEM,
    add_case_pairs,
    add_spectrum,
    build_designspace,
    build_vf,
    instantiate_with_names,
    petal_warp,
    set_metrics,
    set_names,
)

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE = os.path.join(ROOT, "sources", "base")
DONORS = os.path.join(ROOT, "sources", "donors")
MASTERS = os.path.join(ROOT, "sources", "masters")
FONTS = os.path.join(ROOT, "fonts")
PROJECT_URL = "https://github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar"

MANJARI_REGULAR = os.path.join(BASE, "Manjari-Regular.ttf")
MANJARI_BOLD = os.path.join(BASE, "Manjari-Bold.ttf")

# The Malayalam block.  Everything outside it is shared Latin / punctuation /
# symbols in Manjari and is transplanted into every script family.
MALAYALAM_RANGES = [(0x0D00, 0x0D7F)]

NOTO_DEVA = "https://github.com/notofonts/devanagari"
NOTO_TAML = "https://github.com/notofonts/tamil"
NOTO_TELU = "https://github.com/notofonts/telugu"
NOTO_KNDA = "https://github.com/notofonts/kannada"

SCRIPTS = {
    "devanagari": {
        "family": "Kallar Devanagari",
        "name": "कल्लार",
        "stem": "KallarDevanagari",
        "donor": os.path.join(DONORS, "NotoSansDevanagari-VF.ttf"),
        "donor_name": "Noto Sans Devanagari",
        "script_name": "Devanagari",
        "upstream": NOTO_DEVA,
        # Manjari Regular is ~73 units at 1000 UPM and Manjari Bold ~112.
        # The donor's variable axis is instantiated at the closest weight so
        # the script letters share Manjari's pen weight.
        "wght": {400: 360, 700: 550},
        "ranges": [(0x0900, 0x097F), (0xA8E0, 0xA8FF), (0x1CD0, 0x1CFF)],
        "warp": dict(hole_bump=110, peak_bump=60, freeze_above=545,
                     peak_max_y=545, freeze_fade=120, sigma_f=0.22,
                     pinch=0.055, cap_frac=0.55),
        "metrics": dict(asc=800, desc=-300, auto_win=True),
        "display": ["कमल", "द्वार", "नमस्ते"],
        "paragraph": [
            "सभी भाषाएँ सभी लोगों के लिए।",
            "एक लिपि। एक द्वार। एक लोक।",
        ],
        "cases": [
            "नमस्ते", "कमल", "द्वार", "श्री", "क्ष", "त्र", "ज्ञ",
            "संस्कृत", "हिन्दी", "भारत", "कर्म", "धर्म", "बुद्ध",
            "संसार", "कमलम्", "देवनागरी",
        ],
    },
    "tamil": {
        "family": "Kallar Tamil",
        "name": "கல்லார்",
        "stem": "KallarTamil",
        "donor": os.path.join(DONORS, "NotoSansTamil-VF.ttf"),
        "donor_name": "Noto Sans Tamil",
        "script_name": "Tamil",
        "upstream": NOTO_TAML,
        "wght": {400: 360, 700: 550},
        "ranges": [(0x0B80, 0x0BFF)],
        "warp": dict(hole_bump=100, peak_bump=25, freeze_top=0.82,
                     sigma_f=0.30, pinch=0.05, cap_frac=0.55),
        "metrics": dict(asc=800, desc=-300, auto_win=True),
        "display": ["தாமரை", "வாசல்", "வணக்கம்"],
        "paragraph": [
            "எல்லா மொழிகளும் எல்லா மக்களுக்கும்.",
            "ஒரு மொழி. ஒரு வாசல். ஒரு உலகம்.",
        ],
        "cases": [
            "வணக்கம்", "தாமரை", "வாசல்", "தமிழ்", "ஸ்ரீ", "க்ஷ",
            "ஞானம்", "அன்பு", "மனிதம்", "தமிழ்நாடு", "சென்னை",
            "கண்ணன்", "வீடு", "நன்றி",
        ],
    },
    "telugu": {
        "family": "Kallar Telugu",
        "name": "కల్లార్",
        "stem": "KallarTelugu",
        "donor": os.path.join(DONORS, "NotoSansTelugu-VF.ttf"),
        "donor_name": "Noto Sans Telugu",
        "script_name": "Telugu",
        "upstream": NOTO_TELU,
        # Telugu's base stem is heavier, so its donor is instantiated a

# Tables that cannot survive a change of outlines / instancing.
DROP_TABLES = (
    "fvar", "gvar", "avar", "STAT", "HVAR", "MVAR", "VVAR", "DSIG",
    "prep", "fpgm", "cvt ", "VDMX", "hdmx", "LTSH",
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Manjari base
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_manjari(weight=400):
    """Load Manjari at the production UPM, without hinting or variations."""
    path = MANJARI_REGULAR if weight == 400 else MANJARI_BOLD
    font = TTFont(path)
    scale_upem(font, UPEM)
    for tag in DROP_TABLES:
        if tag in font:
            del font[tag]
    # Manjari lacks U+010F/U+01D1; the Malayalam build adds the same two
    # composites, so the shared Latin is complete in every family.
    add_case_pairs(font)
    return font


def unicode_cmap(font):
    cmap = {}
    for table in font["cmap"].tables:
        if table.isUnicode():
            cmap.update(table.cmap)
    return cmap


def manjari_malayalam_glyphs():
    """The GSUB closure of Manjari's Malayalam codepoints.

    These glyphs are not transplanted into the sister families: each family
    carries its own script, and the Malayalam family is the Manjari family.
    """
    font = TTFont(MANJARI_REGULAR)
    codepoints = script_codepoints(font, MALAYALAM_RANGES)
    return script_glyphs(MANJARI_REGULAR, codepoints)


def transplant_manjari(manjari, donor, malayalam_glyphs):
    """Transplant Manjari's shared glyphs into a script donor.

    The donor is used as the shaping container: its glyph order, GSUB/GPOS,
    GDEF and script glyphs stay in place.  Every codepoint outside the
    Malayalam block that Manjari covers is remapped to a Manjari outline,
    using the donor's glyph name where one already exists so the donor's
    layout tables keep working.  Missing Manjari glyphs (and composite
    components) are appended under their Manjari names.
    """
    mglyf = manjari["glyf"]
    dglyf = donor["glyf"]
    mhmtx = manjari["hmtx"]
    dhmtx = donor["hmtx"]
    mcmap = unicode_cmap(manjari)
    dcmap = unicode_cmap(donor)

    order = list(donor.getGlyphOrder())
    names = set(order)
    copied = {}          # (manjari name, donor name) -> True
    dest_by_cp = {}      # codepoint -> donor glyph name

    def unique_name(name):
        if name not in names:
            return name
        i = 1
        while f"kallar.{name}.{i}" in names:
            i += 1
        return f"kallar.{name}.{i}"

    def copy_glyph(src, dst):
        if (src, dst) in copied:
            return
        copied[(src, dst)] = True
        glyph = copy.deepcopy(mglyf[src])
        dglyf[dst] = glyph
        dhmtx.metrics[dst] = mhmtx.metrics[src]
        if dst not in names:
            order.append(dst)
            names.add(dst)
        if glyph.isComposite():
            for component in glyph.components:
                component_name = component.glyphName
                if component_name in mglyf:
                    # Manjari composites reference Manjari components.  Copy
                    # them too so the copied composite is self-contained.
                    copy_glyph(component_name, component_name)

    for cp, manjari_name in sorted(mcmap.items()):
        if any(lo <= cp <= hi for lo, hi in MALAYALAM_RANGES):
            continue
        if manjari_name in malayalam_glyphs:
            continue
        if cp in dcmap:
            dst = dcmap[cp]
        else:
            dst = unique_name(manjari_name)
        copy_glyph(manjari_name, dst)
        dest_by_cp[cp] = dst

    donor.setGlyphOrder(order)
    dglyf.glyphOrder = order
    donor["maxp"].numGlyphs = len(order)
    donor["maxp"].recalc(donor)

    # Rebuild the Unicode cmaps.  Only subtable formats that can represent
    # the codepoint are touched; format 14 is the variation-sequence table.
    for cp, dst in dest_by_cp.items():
        for table in donor["cmap"].tables:
            if not table.isUnicode() or table.format == 14:
                continue
            if table.format == 4 and cp > 0xFFFF:
                continue
            if table.format in (0, 6):
                continue
            table.cmap[cp] = dst

    # Keep GDEF classes for the transplanted glyphs.  This matters for
    # combining marks such as Manjari's zero-width caron.
    if "GDEF" in donor and "GDEF" in manjari:
        dgdef = donor["GDEF"].table
        mgdef = manjari["GDEF"].table
        dclasses = getattr(dgdef, "GlyphClassDef", None)
        mclasses = getattr(mgdef, "GlyphClassDef", None)
        if dclasses is not None and mclasses is not None:
            for (src, dst) in copied:
                cls = mclasses.classDefs.get(src)
                if cls is not None:
                    dclasses.classDefs[dst] = cls

    return donor


def instantiate_base(script, weight):
    out = os.path.join(
        MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style_for(weight)}-Round.ttf"
    )
    manjari = load_manjari(weight)
    donor = TTFont(script["donor"])
    instantiateVariableFont(
        donor, {"wght": script["wght"][weight], "wdth": 100}, inplace=True
    )
    for tag in DROP_TABLES:
        if tag in donor:
            del donor[tag]
    scale_upem(donor, UPEM)
    font = transplant_manjari(manjari, donor, manjari_malayalam_glyphs())
    style = style_for(weight)
    set_names(
        font, script["family"], style, weight=weight,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script),
        url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    set_metrics(font, weight=weight, **script["metrics"])
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(out)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# donor helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def script_codepoints(font, ranges):
    cps = set()
    for table in font["cmap"].tables:
        if not table.isUnicode():
            continue
        for cp in table.cmap:
            if any(lo <= cp <= hi for lo, hi in ranges):
                cps.add(cp)
    return cps


def script_glyphs(path, codepoints):
    """Return the GSUB closure of a script's codepoints.

    Using fontTools' subsetter closure means conjuncts, half forms, reph forms
    and contextual variants are all included, while Latin, punctuation and
    unrelated glyphs are left in the base style.
    """
    font = TTFont(path)
    opts = subset.Options()
    opts.layout_features = ["*"]
    opts.notdef_outline = True
    opts.recalc_bounds = False
    opts.drop_tables = []
    subsetter = subset.Subsetter(opts)
    subsetter.populate(unicodes=codepoints)
    subsetter.subset(font)
    names = set(font.getGlyphOrder())
    names.discard(".notdef")
    return names


def copyright_for(script):
    return (
        "Copyright 2026 The Kallar Project Authors. "
        "Base skeleton: Manjari, Copyright 2018 The Manjari Project Authors "
        "(https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/manjari, OFL-1.1). "
        f"{script['script_name']} letter structures adapted from "
        f"{script['donor_name']}, Copyright 2022 The Noto Project Authors "
        f"({script['upstream']}, OFL-1.1)."
    )


def designer_for(script):
    return (
        "Kallar Project Authors; base design by Santhosh Thottingal (SMC); "
        f"{script['script_name']} letter structures adapted from the "
        "Noto Project Authors"
    )


def style_for(weight):
    return "Regular" if weight == 400 else "Bold"


def make_petal(round_path, petal_path, glyphs, warp):
    font = TTFont(round_path)
    petal_warp(font, only=glyphs, **warp)
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(petal_path)
    return petal_path


def to_woff2(path):
    font = TTFont(path)
    font.flavor = "woff2"
    font.recalcTimestamp = False
    font.save(path[:-4] + ".woff2")
    return path[:-4] + ".woff2"


def build_script(key):
    script = SCRIPTS[key]
    os.makedirs(MASTERS, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(FONTS, exist_ok=True)

    # The Malayalam closure is stable across weights; compute it once.
    malayalam_glyphs = manjari_malayalam_glyphs()

    paths = []
    vfs = {}
    for weight in (400, 700):
        style = style_for(weight)
        round_path = instantiate_base(script, weight)
        if weight == 400:
            cps = script_codepoints(TTFont(round_path), script["ranges"])
            glyphs = script_glyphs(round_path, cps)
            # Never warp a glyph transplanted from Manjari's shared set.
            glyphs -= unicode_cmap(TTFont(round_path)).values()
            glyphs -= malayalam_glyphs
            print(f"{key}: {len(cps)} codepoints, {len(glyphs)} glyphs in closure")
        petal_path = os.path.join(
            MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}-Petal.ttf"
        )
        make_petal(round_path, petal_path, glyphs, script["warp"])
        ds_path = os.path.join(MASTERS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}.designspace")
        build_designspace(
            round_path, petal_path, ds_path,
            family=script["family"], style=style,
        )
        vf_path = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-{style}.ttf")
        build_vf(
            ds_path, vf_path,
            family=script["family"], style=style,
            metrics=script["metrics"],
            copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
            designer=designer_for(script),
            url=PROJECT_URL,
            stat_values=[
                dict(value=0, name="0", flags=0x2),
                dict(value=50, name="50"),
                dict(value=100, name="100"),
            ],
        )
        paths.append(vf_path)
        vfs[weight] = vf_path

    # COLRv1 Spectrum, Regular and Bold
    spectrum_reg = os.path.join(
        FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-SpectrumRegular.ttf"
    )
    spectrum_bold = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Spectrum.ttf")
    add_spectrum(
        vfs[400], spectrum_reg,
        family=f"{script['family']} Spectrum", style="Regular", weight=400,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    add_spectrum(
        vfs[700], spectrum_bold,
        family=f"{script['family']} Spectrum", style="Bold", weight=700,
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    paths.extend([spectrum_reg, spectrum_bold])

    # Static APER instances, following the Malayalam naming model.
    round_static = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Round.ttf")
    petal_static = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-Petal.ttf")
    bold_petal = os.path.join(FONTS, f"{script['stem']}-BoldPetal.ttf")
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[400], round_static, {"APER": 0},
        f"{script['family']} Round", "Regular",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[400], petal_static, {"APER": 100},
        f"{script['family']} Petal", "Regular",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    instantiate_with_names(
        vfs[700], bold_petal, {"APER": 100},
        f"{script['family']} Petal", "Bold",
        copyright_note=copyright_for(script),
        designer=designer_for(script), url=PROJECT_URL,
    )
    paths.extend([round_static, petal_static, bold_petal])

    for path in paths:
        to_woff2(path)
    print(f"{key}: wrote {len(paths)} TTF + WOFF2 files")
    return paths


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument(
        "scripts", nargs="*",
        help=f"script families to build (default: all): {', '.join(sorted(SCRIPTS))}",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    unknown = [s for s in args.scripts if s not in SCRIPTS]
    if unknown:
        ap.error(f"unknown script(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
    selected = args.scripts or list(SCRIPTS)
    for key in selected:
        build_script(key)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
