# Manjari base

**Manjari is the base skeleton of every Kallar family.** The shared Latin,
digits, punctuation, symbols, spacing, metrics and design language all come
from these two files. The Malayalam family is Manjari throughout.

| Branch | Upstream | Vendored files | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | [Manjari](https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/manjari) by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC | `Manjari-Regular.ttf`, `Manjari-Bold.ttf` | `164609…0f95` (Regular), `f19fef…9d26` (Bold) |

The full checksums are in `AUTHORS.md`.

## Script donors

Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, so it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
Kannada outlines. The four sister families use the corresponding Noto Sans
faces as **script donors**. A donor supplies only the script-specific letter
structures and the GSUB/GPOS rules that shape them; every shared glyph is
transplanted from Manjari. The donors are vendored in
[`sources/donors/`](../donors/) with their upstream OFL texts.

## Derivative model

All five Kallar families are derivatives of Manjari. Each family is renamed to
`Kallar` or `Kallar <Script>`, preserves the Manjari copyright and OFL notice,
and records the base in its name table and documentation. The Devanagari,
Tamil, Telugu and Kannada letter structures are adapted from the Noto Sans
donors under the SIL Open Font License; that attribution is kept in every
derived font. The aperture axis, the Spectrum treatment and the specimens are
original work by the Kallar Project Authors.

This project is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google,
the Noto Project Authors, Sarvam AI, or SMC.

# Script donors

Manjari is the base skeleton of every Kallar family, but it contains only
Malayalam and Latin glyphs. The four sister scripts therefore use the Noto
Sans faces below as **script donors**: the donor supplies only the
script-specific letter structures and shaping rules, while the shared glyphs
and the design language are transplanted from Manjari.

| Script | Upstream | Vendored file | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Devanagari | [Noto Sans Devanagari](https://github.com/notofonts/devanagari) | `NotoSansDevanagari-VF.ttf` | `14ec4af41f27482216d1c2229f417ff9b1425e1babb014e57d1d40d03229853e` |
| Tamil | [Noto Sans Tamil](https://github.com/notofonts/tamil) | `NotoSansTamil-VF.ttf` | `aa3a9b321f4b0bb2c40203ffbde9af89713227866e0e13f76e5b9eeea727cf88` |
| Telugu | [Noto Sans Telugu](https://github.com/notofonts/telugu) | `NotoSansTelugu-VF.ttf` | `e618af7bf999df192ed4f388eba2e563f2b5015034e9cbb317b5bd793bd7334d` |
| Kannada | [Noto Sans Kannada](https://github.com/notofonts/kannada) | `NotoSansKannada-VF.ttf` | `cca4f3b3a8cb12fb261f1b43baf5d2f7f59d90fe123d41f0065ed3a183997ec9` |

The variable fonts were downloaded from the `google/fonts` repository on
2026-11-09. They are vendored so that builds are offline and reproducible.
Each upstream font carries its own copyright notice in its `name` table and
its own `OFL.txt` beside the binary.

## How a donor is used

1. The variable donor is instantiated at the weight that matches Manjari's
   pen: `wght=360` for Regular and `wght=550` for Bold (Telugu uses
   `340`/`500` because its base stem is heavier).
2. The donor is used as the shaping container; its GSUB/GPOS, GDEF and
   script glyphs stay in place.
3. Every codepoint outside the Malayalam block that Manjari covers is
   remapped to a Manjari outline. The shared Latin, digits, punctuation and
   spacing in the output are therefore Manjari's.
4. The script GSUB closure is warped along the `APER` axis. The donor's
   shared Latin is never warped.

The donor is not the base. It is a source of script-specific letter
structures that Manjari does not contain.

# Authors & credits

## Kallar

- **Design, aperture engine, variable font, Spectrum build, specimen:**
  Kallar Project Authors, 2026.
- **Base skeleton for every family:** Manjari by **Santhosh Thottingal** and
  **Swathanthra Malayalam Computing** (SMC), Copyright 2018 The Manjari
  Project Authors. Licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
  <https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/manjari>
  Manjari supplies the shared Latin, digits, punctuation, symbols, spacing,
  metrics and design language of all five Kallar families.
- **Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada script donors:** Noto Sans
  Devanagari, Noto Sans Tamil, Noto Sans Telugu and Noto Sans Kannada by
  **The Noto Project Authors**, Copyright 2022. Licensed under the SIL Open
  Font License 1.1. <https://github.com/notofonts>
  The donors supply only the script-specific letter structures that Manjari
  does not contain; they are not the base of the family.
- **Legacy v0.2 parametric draft / shaping engine:** adapted from
  **Nupuram** by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC, Copyright 2023 The Nupuram Project
  Authors, MIT. <https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/Nupuram>
- **Sarvam inspiration:** the blue → orange spectrum and the gateway/lotus
  visual language are an homage to [Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand).
  This project is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by
  Sarvam AI.

## License

The font software and sources are released under the **SIL Open Font License
1.1**. See [OFL.txt](OFL.txt). The legacy build tools retain their MIT
attribution in the source files.

## Vendored base checksums

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `sources/base/Manjari-Regular.ttf` | `16460924696bfea2a2f71b4201d8786867c6413b548ecbd22bc6bfe55be90f95` |
| `sources/base/Manjari-Bold.ttf` | `f19fef695b28e5448ae87451dfbab426676cadf4b59340558a157c0071b69d26` |

The script donors and their checksums are documented in
[`sources/donors/README.md`](sources/donors/README.md).

## 9. The multiscript extension

### 9.1 Manjari is the base of every family

The original idea is preserved: all five Kallar families start from the
**Manjari** skeleton. Manjari supplies the shared Latin, digits, punctuation,
symbols, spacing, metrics and design language. The Malayalam family is Manjari
throughout.

Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, so it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
Kannada glyphs. Drawing four new scripts from a blank page would be a
years-long design project, and a from-scratch skeleton would not have Manjari's
quality. The release therefore uses one OFL **script donor** per
non-Malayalam script. The donor supplies only the script-specific letter
structures and shaping rules; it is not the base. Every shared glyph is
transplanted from Manjari, and the donor is instantiated at the weight that
matches Manjari's pen.

The four families are deliberately separate variable fonts rather than one
merged font. Scripts have different GSUB/GPOS tables, glyph names, mark
attachments and vertical metrics; merging them would create conflicts in
shared Latin, punctuation and mark glyphs. Separate families also match how
Anek, Noto and most multiscript systems ship, and let each script keep its own
line height.

### 9.2 Sources

| Branch | Base | Script donor | Upstream |
|---|---|---|---|
| Malayalam | Manjari | — | smc/fonts/manjari |
| Devanagari | Manjari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari |
| Tamil | Manjari | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil |
| Telugu | Manjari | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu |
| Kannada | Manjari | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada |

The donor variable fonts are instantiated at the weight that matches
Manjari's stroke: `wght=360` for Regular and `wght=550` for Bold (Telugu uses
`340`/`500` because its base stem is heavier). They are then stripped of
hinting and variation tables and scaled to 1000 UPM (they are already 1000).
The Manjari base is scaled to 1000 UPM, stripped of hinting, and given the two
Latin case pairs (U+010F, U+01D1) that Manjari lacks. The vendored files and
SHA-256 checksums are in `sources/base/README.md` and
`sources/donors/README.md`.

## 9. The multiscript extension

### 9.1 Why separate families

Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face; it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
Kannada glyphs. A literal Manjari derivative therefore cannot cover those
scripts. The multiscript release uses one OFL skeleton per script and keeps the
same derivative model: rename, preserve the upstream copyright, record the
base, and do the new work in the aperture engine, axis, Spectrum, metrics and
specimens.

The four new families are deliberately separate variable fonts rather than one
merged font. Scripts have different GSUB/GPOS tables, glyph names, mark
attachments and vertical metrics; merging them would create conflicts in
shared Latin, punctuation and mark glyphs. Separate families also match how
Anek, Noto and most multiscript systems ship, and let each script keep its own
line height.

### 9.2 Sources

| Branch | Base | Upstream |
|---|---|---|
| Devanagari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari |
| Tamil | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil |
| Telugu | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu |
| Kannada | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada |

The variable bases are instantiated at `wght=400/700`, `wdth=100`, scaled to
1000 UPM (they are already 1000), stripped of hinting and variation tables, and
given the Kallar name/metrics. The vendored files and SHA-256 checksums are in
`sources/base/README.md`.

input.newString:
### 9.4 Glyph filtering

`tools/multiscript.py` first transplants every Manjari codepoint outside the
Malayalam block into the donor, using the donor's glyph name where one already
exists so the donor's GSUB/GPOS keeps working. Missing Manjari glyphs are
appended. Composites are flattened during the transplant, so a Manjari
composite cannot become a nested component inside a donor composite.

`petal_warp` then accepts `only`, a set of glyph names. The build computes that
set with `fontTools.subset`: it starts from the script's codepoints and closes
over GSUB, so conjuncts, half forms, reph forms, contextual variants and matras
are included. The Manjari shared set is subtracted, so Latin, punctuation and
digits stay in Manjari's style and are never warped.

The closure sizes (excluding `.notdef`) are 735 Devanagari, 166 Tamil, 723
Telugu and 414 Kannada glyphs.

input.newString:
### 9.5 Metrics

The families use Manjari's typographic metrics (`sTypoAscender=800`,
`sTypoDescender=-300`, `sTypoLineGap=0`) so the shared Latin and the script
text sit on one line-height system. The win metrics are computed from the
actual outline extents, because the script donors have marks that reach above
and below Manjari's Latin:

```
usWinAscent  = max(sTypoAscender, ceil(yMax) + 50)
usWinDescent = max(-sTypoDescender, ceil(-yMin) + 50)
```

Devanagari's Vedic marks reach y=1347, so its win ascent is 1397; the typo
ascender stays at Manjari's 800, which means fontbakery reports the expected
`typoAscender` warning for the tall Manjari `Agrave` and Vedic marks. All
families set `USE_TYPO_METRICS`.

Inherited donor warnings (not introduced by this project) include:

- GDEF mark-class warnings for Vedic characters;
- a missing `avar` table (the APER axis is linear, so no mapping is needed);
- long Vedic glyph names and unreachable Vedic variants;
- a soft hyphen in the donor font;
- a `typoAscender` warning because Manjari's tall accented Latin and the
  Vedic marks extend above the 800-unit typo ascender. The win metrics are
  computed from the actual extents, so nothing clips.

These are recorded rather than silenced, because changing GDEF classes or
removing Vedic glyphs could break shaping.

### 9.7 Multiscript limits

- Manjari contains no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or Kannada outlines. The
  script-specific letters therefore come from the Noto donors; only the
  shared glyphs and the design system are literally Manjari. A future release
  could draw those letters from Manjari's pen, but that is a new type-design
  project, not a build change.
- The donor's Latin kerning lookups still apply to the transplanted Manjari
  advances. The kerning is close, but a few pairs may need Manjari-specific
  values; importing Manjari's `latn` GPOS would be the next refinement.
- Tamil has fewer closed counters than the other scripts, so its APER change
  is deliberately subtler. A more radical Tamil cut would need new stroke
  terminals, not just a counter warp.
- The four families are separate fonts. A merged all-in-one font is not
  planned because of the shaping and glyph-name conflicts described above.
- The Spectrum gradient is the same font-unit range for every script; a
  per-script baseline calibration could be a future refinement.

content.text:
Implemented. Manjari is now the base of every Kallar family, not just Malayalam.

### What changed

- **Every family starts from Manjari.** The build now loads `Manjari-Regular/Bold`, transplants Manjari’s shared glyphs into each script family, and keeps Manjari’s:
  - Latin letters, digits, punctuation and symbols
  - word-space and advance widths
  - Latin kerning lookups
  - typographic metrics (`800/-300`) and OS/2 x-height/cap-height
- **Noto is no longer the base.** The Noto Sans files were moved from `sources/base/` to `sources/donors/` and are now used only as **script donors** for the Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada letter structures that Manjari does not contain.
- **Donor weights are calibrated to Manjari’s pen**: `wght=360/550` for Devanagari, Tamil and Kannada; `340/500` for Telugu.
- **Composites are flattened** during the transplant, so Manjari composites do not become nested components inside donor composites.
- **Metadata, tests and docs updated**:
  - `README.md` now shows `Base: Manjari` for all five families and explains the donor model.
  - `NOTES.md`, `AUTHORS.md`, `FONTLOG.txt`, `OFL.txt`, `sources/base/README.md` and the new `sources/donors/README.md` all reflect the new derivative model.
  - `tests/test_multiscript.py` now verifies that `H`, `a`, `0`, `.`, the word space and Latin kern pairs are Manjari’s in every family.
  - Specimens and PDFs were regenerated.

### Verification

- `make test` → exit 0, all three suites pass.
- `make qa-multiscript` → **0 FAIL** on all eight Regular/Bold variable fonts.
- Repeated `make multiscript` runs produce byte-identical fonts.
- `git diff --check` clean.

One honest technical note: Manjari has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or Kannada glyphs, so a literal all-Manjari outline source for those scripts is impossible without drawing four new scripts from scratch. The current implementation makes Manjari the base for everything it actually contains — shared glyphs, spacing, kerning, metrics and design language — while Noto supplies only the script-specific letters, clearly documented as donors. The changes are in the working tree and not committed.
Update README with new version and push it to github
